_note: What nomad-watch checks. Order is roughly 'what hurts most when it dies quietly'.
type=heartbeat is the only kind that proves a service is still DOING its job; the rest prove
it is reachable, which is weaker. Add a heartbeat for anything whose failure is silent.
`hint` is printed inside the alert, so it should say the first thing to try, not describe
the problem again. Set enabled:false to mute a target without losing why it was here.

targets.name: relay loop
targets.hint: The relay is `active` but not polling the engine. `journalctl --user -u nomad-relay -n 50`; a Zulip key rotation exits 3 and self-heals, anything else does not.

targets.name: engine stall sweep
targets.hint: The thread that fails runs abandoned in `new` has stopped, while the container stays up. Runs can sit in `new` forever with nobody waiting. `docker compose logs nomad-v2-engine | grep sweep`.

targets.name: nomad-relay unit
targets.hint: `systemctl --user status nomad-relay`. In `failed` after ~2 minutes means the Zulip key is wrong, not stale.

targets.name: dispatcher
targets.hint: `systemctl --user status nomad-dispatch`. It exits on purpose if it cannot read ~/.config/nomad/dispatch-token.

targets.name: autopilot supervisor
targets.hint: The heartbeat moves only when a whole pass ends, so a high age means a pass is hung; refused means the daemon is down. `journalctl --user -u nomad-autopilot -n 50`, then `systemctl --user restart nomad-autopilot`: running workers survive the restart and are adopted.

targets.name: v2 engine
targets.hint: The pipeline. `docker compose logs --tail=50 nomad-v2-engine`.

targets.name: n8n gate webhook
targets.hint: 404 here means the Approval Gate workflow is DEACTIVATED, not that n8n is down. This is the outage that hid for three and a half months. `n8n update:workflow --active=true`.

targets.name: n8n
targets.hint: Owns the gate, the workflows and the credentials. `docker logs nomad-n8n-standalone --tail=50`.

targets.name: LiteLLM gateway
targets.hint: Every model call goes through here. Recreate, never restart: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate litellm`.

targets.name: NocoDB
targets.hint: v2 mission control. `docker logs nomad-nocodb --tail=50`.

targets.name: console
targets._why_off: v1 nomad-console stopped on purpose 2026-10-02 (#350). Removal from compose is #351; drop this target then.
targets.hint: `docker compose logs --tail=50 nomad-console`.

targets.name: Zulip
targets.hint: If this is down the watchdog cannot report anything, so its own pass will fail too.

targets.name: postgres
targets.hint: `nomad_v2` lives here. Everything v2 stops without it.

targets.name: qdrant
targets.hint: `nomad_memory`. Memory reads fail soft, so its death is silent.

targets.name: termd
targets.hint: `systemctl --user status nomad-term`.

targets.name: nomad-voice
targets.hint: `systemctl --user status nomad-voice`.

targets.name: nomad-detect
targets.hint: Keep it bound to localhost. `systemctl --user status nomad-detect`.

targets.name: nomad-scraper
targets.hint: Research lane grounding (ADR-007). `docker logs nomad-scraper --tail=50`.

targets.name: OpenProject API
targets.hint: nomad-pm, the work tracker (ADR-011). 401 means it answered and wants a token. Otherwise `cd ~/nomad-pm && docker compose ps && docker compose logs --tail 50 openproject`. A 400 means the Host header is not in OPENPROJECT_ADDITIONAL__HOST__NAMES, which is why this uses localhost, not 127.0.0.1.

targets.name: nomad-pm backup
targets.hint: The nightly OpenProject backup has not succeeded in 30 hours. `journalctl --user -u nomad-pm-backup -n 30`, then rerun with `systemctl --user start nomad-pm-backup`. Backups are in ~/backups/nomad-pm.

targets.name: vault (openbao)
targets.hint: Sealed (503) or down. `docker ps | grep vault`; `systemctl --user status nomad-vault-unseal`; `~/nomad/vault/unseal.sh`. Google MCP is down until it is unsealed.

targets.name: vault backup
targets.hint: The nightly OpenBao raft snapshot did not run. `systemctl --user status nomad-vault-backup.service`; `~/nomad/vault/backup.sh`.
